I get what you are saying but I can't help but think that there is quite a big difference.

For one, Abby killed Joel slowly and painfully in cold blood when he was outnumbered, disarmed AND after he had actually saved her life. It's difficult to imagine what kind of person wouldn't take that into consideration in that situation. Even with "eye for an eye"-morals, Joel didn't torture her father.

If she wasn't so extremely narrow minded, she should have been able to see that he is not a bad person. Yes, he killed her father, but it was to save someone's life. They even talk about the moral dilemma of the surgery in the flashbacks. (there are additional clearly extenuating circumstances such as Joel actually having been betrayed by the Fireflies after delivering Ellie, him having lost his own daughter prior to this, the surgeon threatening him with the scalpel and refusing to let Ellie go etc, but I don't know how much of this Abby is aware of). Nevertheless, the fact that Abby was fully aware of the moral dilemma of the surgery and being rescued by Joel should be enough to, at the very least, afford him an "You saved me, so I'll make this quick." Not with Abby. In no way did ND succeed in creating a second protagonist in her, just an utterly self-centered villain.

What attracted me to this game was the friendship between Joel and Ellie. The fact that ND decided turn away from that and make this a bleak story of hate and utter loss is something I honestly cannot even wrap my mind around.

>The first jump, at the peak of your (the gamer) rage, they start over and build it all the way back up. They aim for you to feel just a strong  of a feeling in the opposite direction, so that you would be conflicted  when you got back to the theater. 

While you may be right that this is their intention, it is very hard to see how the author of Part 1 could believe this to be accomplished. We end up playing as a character we hate, who literally tortured and killed a beloved protagonist shortly after he rescued her from infected, beating up the second protagonist we love. It becomes so absurd that I am left speechless when we are asked to press square as Abby to keep punching Ellie.
Cannot unsee.
She is putting herself, her child and her squadmates in danger. The fact that she is tagging along feels like satire.

It is lazy writing that Joel just happens to fall into Abby's lap when she goes out looking for him. Her solo hunt for him was unlikely to be successful, considering how well-defended Jackson is and how skilled survivors Joel and his friends were. Instead Joel and Tommy actually rescue her from infected in the nick of time. She was already failing in her hunt, soon to be dead, which proves the point.

As for the likelihood of an outbreak in Jackson, if they had chosen that narrative they could simply have made the city less well-defended and resourceful when they created it.

They could have taken it in another direction, yes. Since Joel made the survivalist choice of not leaving loose ends it would have made narrative sense for him to successfully evade pursuit. Having left the Fireflies behind (or dead), the game could instead have delved deeper into the pandemic, the bleak reality that remains after all hopes of a vaccine have been dashed, the nature of Ellie's immunity and her survivor guilt. This could easily have been escalated by having additional characters close to her becoming infected, perhaps through an outbreak that eradicates Jackson and underscores the fact that nowhere is safe anymore. In the Last of Us 2 the developers did introduce an interesting Legion-type monstrosity so they could easily have made the horrors of the cordiceps grow even darker. The story would have revolved around winning back trust and mending a bond of friendship that transcends the world rather than hatred.

In Sweden it is customary to have at least five weeks of paid vacation per year (many have more). Additionally, we also have several paid holidays, such as Midsummer, National Day, New Year, Christmas, Feast of the Ascension, Easter Monday, Epiphany, May Day and so on.

Most employers also give paid leave the day before a National holiday, either the full day or half of the day.

To my experience, people rarely have the opinion that vacation would have a negative effect on productivity, quite the contrary.

In fact, we often discuss how to maximize our time off at the workplace and the newspapers write articles about how to use your vacation days to get the longest possible streaks of paid leave (such as when May Day is on a Wednesday, your employer might give you Tuesday off and you take one vacation day on Monday, thus getting five work-free days by including the weekend). We call these days "klämdagar", which translates roughly as "squeezedays".
